newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers flat-up on supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Basis offers flat-up on supply.

text.p: Soymeal supplies in domestic markets remained tight Wednesday, and basis offers were steady to slightly higher as a result, soymeal brokers said.
"The market is still good," one Minnesota-based broker said. "If you have meal to sell, there's somebody out there who will buy it."
Domestic end-users were still seen purchasing soymeal on a "hand-to-mouth" or as-needed basis, but a drop in prices could spur heavy buying, brokers said.

Booming exports were said to be the reason that the market is so tight, but some dealers expect that pace to slow soon. "Some folks are thinking the (export) market is going to back off a little bit," one river broker said.

Solid gains in CBOT soymeal futures also captured the attention of cash meal brokers. Futures rallied in response to a bullish crop production estimate of 2.367 billion bushels from consultants Sparks Cos. of Memphis, Tenn., traders said. At 1020 CST, CBOT December soymeal was up $2.10 per ton at $222.60, and other months were up $0.50 to $2.20 per ton.
